input.summary: The paper claim asserts that adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions. The user asks whether a single completed emulated trial can prove this caused higher performance for all Internet users. The short answer is: no — a single emulated pilot trial cannot establish causality or generalize to all Internet users. This proposal designs a bounded emulated-netem-v1 pilot to measure the directional effect of 20 ms added delay on flow completion time (FCT) under controlled conditions, while explicitly scoping what such a pilot can and cannot conclude. Key gaps include: unknown bottleneck rate, buffer size, file sizes, and CCA(s) intended by the original claim; no full paper text is available; and the claim's directionality ("changes") is underspecified. The pilot is proposed as a first step toward characterizing the effect size and variance under one set of emulated conditions only.
questions: What bottleneck rate (Mbit/s), buffer size (kbytes), file size(s) (MBytes), and congestion control algorithm(s) were used or intended in the original claim's emulated setup?
Does 'changes' in the claim mean an increase, a decrease, or simply a statistically detectable difference in flow completion time — and is there a specific magnitude or direction the paper reports?

Is the owner prepared to accept a proposed emulated-netem-v1 pilot with the placeholder conditions below (e.g., 10 Mbit/s bottleneck, 200 kbyte buffer, 10 MByte file, cubic CCA, 0% loss), or should different values be substituted before freezing?

proposal.problem: The claim states that adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions. It is unknown whether this effect is positive or negative, what magnitude is expected, and whether any single emulated trial can generalize beyond its specific configuration. The full paper text and exact experimental parameters are unavailable (source sha256: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa; packet sha256: a1b401caab0920ee2f11377b7285ff0ef7269c187cfa7f3df1c1cb576ba8c0da).
proposal.question: Under a specific set of fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, does adding 20 ms of one-way client delay produce a measurable difference in TCP flow completion time compared to 0 ms added delay — and can such a result generalize to all Internet users?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Proposed (placeholder) emulated conditions: 2 clients; one arm at 0 ms added delay (control), one arm at 20 ms added delay (treatment); CCA = cubic; file size = 10 MBytes per flow; bottleneck rate = 10 Mbit/s; bottleneck buffer = 200 kbytes; loss = 0%; snapshot interval = 100 ms. These values are proposals pending owner confirmation. Actual paper conditions are unknown due to missing full text.
proposal.related_work: TCP flow completion time is known to increase with round-trip time (RTT) due to slower slow-start ramp-up, larger congestion windows required, and more ACK-clocking delay. The magnitude depends on file size, bottleneck capacity, buffer size, and CCA. Emulated network testbeds (e.g., netem) are standard for controlled FCT measurement but do not replicate the heterogeneity of real Internet paths, middleboxes, cross-traffic, or diverse receiver hardware. Source citation: 'Synthetic networking paper claim for development evaluation' (sha256: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa). No full text was available for review.
proposal.alternatives: 1. The 20 ms delay has no practically significant effect on FCT at the tested file size and bottleneck rate (null effect). 2. The effect exists but is CCA-specific (e.g., BBR compensates better than cubic). 3. The effect is detectable in emulation but absent or reversed in real-world conditions due to bufferbloat, path asymmetry, or receiver-window scaling. 4. The direction of 'changes' is a decrease (e.g., if pacing or slow-start interacts unexpectedly with the added delay).
proposal.design: Proposed pilot design (emulated-netem-v1): Two-arm within-emulation comparison. Arm A (control): 2 clients, 0 ms added delay, cubic CCA, 10 MByte file, 10 Mbit/s bottleneck, 200 kbyte buffer, 0% loss. Arm B (treatment): identical except 20 ms added delay per client. 16 replications per arm (32 total planned units). Primary metric: flow_completion_time_ms per client per replication. This is a pilot (stage: pilot); it cannot establish causality for all Internet users. Broader validation would require: multiple CCAs, multiple file sizes, multiple bottleneck rates, real-world iperf measurements, and diverse network paths.
proposal.metrics: Primary: flow_completion_time_ms (milliseconds) per flow per replication. Secondary: difference in mean FCT between 0 ms and 20 ms arms. No inferential confidence intervals are declared without a justified independent sampling design; descriptive ranges (min, median, max, IQR) will be reported per arm.
proposal.controls: Fixed across both arms: bottleneck rate (10 Mbit/s proposed), bottleneck buffer (200 kbytes proposed), file size (10 MBytes proposed), CCA (cubic proposed), loss rate (0%), number of clients (2), snapshot interval (100 ms), emulation environment version (emulated-netem-v1). Replications randomized in order. No cross-traffic injected.
proposal.falsification: The claim is not falsified if FCT differs between 0 ms and 20 ms arms in the expected direction. The claim is challenged (but not definitively falsified) if: (a) FCT distributions overlap completely across all 16 replications per arm, or (b) the median FCT difference is less than 1% of the control arm median. A single pilot cannot falsify the claim for all Internet users regardless of outcome.
proposal.inputs: Required: emulated-netem-v1 runner; netem_nines.py script (version unspecified, hash unknown — must be supplied by owner before freezing). Paper source sha256: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa (full text not available). Packet sha256: a1b401caab0920ee2f11377b7285ff0ef7269c187cfa7f3df1c1cb576ba8c0da. Bottleneck rate, buffer, file size, and CCA are proposed placeholders; owner must confirm or replace.
proposal.limitations: 1. A single emulated pilot cannot prove causality for all Internet users — emulation lacks real-world heterogeneity (diverse RTTs, cross-traffic, middleboxes, receiver diversity, wireless links). 2. Full paper text is unavailable; the exact intended conditions, directionality, and magnitude of the claim are unknown. 3. Placeholder configuration values may not match the paper's setup. 4. 16 replications per arm provides limited power for small effect sizes. 5. Fresh AI reviews of this proposal share models and inputs and are not independent human review. 6. Success in this pilot cannot establish generalization beyond the tested configuration.

questions: What bottleneck rate, buffer size, file size(s), and CCA(s) were used in the original claim?
Is the directionality of 'changes' specified (increase or decrease) in the paper?
Does the owner confirm the proposed placeholder conditions for the pilot?
protocol.hypotheses: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.

metrics.name: flow_completion_time_ms
metrics.criterion: Median FCT in 20 ms arm differs from median FCT in 0 ms arm by more than 1% of the 0 ms arm median across 16 replications

input_versions.sha256: <UNKNOWN — must be supplied by owner before freezing>

protocol.dates_or_epochs: To be recorded at execution time; not pre-specified.
protocol.seeds: Not applicable to netem emulation timing; replication order randomized if supported by runner.

sensitivity.rationale: FCT is sensitive to bottleneck rate, buffer size, file size, and CCA. Results under placeholder conditions may not replicate under the paper's actual conditions. A sensitivity sweep over at least two file sizes and two CCAs is recommended in a follow-on main experiment.

protocol.replication_unit: One full emulated flow completion per client per run
protocol.sample_size_rationale: 16 replications per arm (2 configurations × 16 = 32 planned units, within the ≤32 limit). Sufficient for descriptive characterization of FCT distributions; not powered for formal hypothesis testing without effect size estimates from the paper.
protocol.exclusions: Replications where any client FCT is reported as 0 ms or missing will be flagged and excluded from summary statistics.
protocol.missing_data: If fewer than 12 of 16 replications complete per arm, the pilot will be reported as inconclusive and the owner notified.
protocol.statistics: Descriptive only: median, IQR, min, max of flow_completion_time_ms per arm. No inferential intervals declared. Difference in medians reported as absolute (ms) and relative (%) of control arm median.
protocol.dependence: Replications within the same emulated environment may share system state; treated as independent for descriptive purposes only. Temporal ordering of replications recorded.

resource_limits.cost_basis: Emulated runner; no cloud cost model available. Cost unknown.

protocol.stopping_rule: Stop after 32 planned units or if wall_seconds limit is reached. No adaptive stopping based on interim results.
protocol.prior_exposure: This proposal was drafted without prior execution of this experiment. No results have been observed.
protocol.coverage_limits: Results apply only to the specific emulated configuration tested. No generalization to real Internet users, other CCAs, other file sizes, or other bottleneck rates is warranted from this pilot alone.
protocol.data_origin: Emulated synthetic network traffic generated by emulated-netem-v1 runner. Not real-world Internet measurements.
